correctness_confidence.basis: At half noise the 21/8 to 15/2 step saturates the hypercontractivity relation. Substituting the entropy cost and the shell factors gives a strictly negative log base.

rigor.basis: The symmetric killed matrix and its positive test vector justify the row estimate even for arbitrary subsets. The sign construction compares the same stationary denominator and controls the quadratic remainder uniformly in dimension.

significance.basis: The result decides the relative-conductance question on the exhibited half-noise balls and eliminates matching there. The explicit sufficient radius is small and no global mixing or gap bound follows.

summary: First assessment of the five-page PDF. I checked the limits of the conductance comparison, the strict radial counterexample and the coordinate projection argument. I recommend circulation as a working paper. The mathematical advance concerns local exit at a specified noise level. The importance score reflects that limited scope. I took part in preparation and saw the source verification and earlier programme work before reviewing the rendered artifact.
strengths: Page 2. Applying the floor before Jensen bounds the reciprocal at every vertex. The separate Schur weight uses the location of the center and preserves the stationary L3 budget.
Pages 3 and 4. Odd radii pair the shells, and the transition likelihood ratio makes the last negative shell dominate. The unperturbed ball comparison alone would not give this sign.
Pages 4 and 5. Cauchy–Schwarz after inversion only on queried coordinates gives a multiplicative bound even for rare pair atoms; the leaf-pair union needs at most twice the tree depth.
weaknesses: The rate and radius are sufficient constants. The proof cannot exclude relative conductance changes for substantially larger balls or for general correlation.

The strict sign example alone gives no lower bound of constant order on the relative retention discrepancy. The conductance corollary compares complements and should not be applied to ratios of the two small retentions.

Page 4 contains one long inline identity reaching into the right margin. All five page images are legible, including the end of that identity. The prior-art search does not certify priority and there has been no independent replication or formal proof check.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exponential escape for arbitrary potentials under a stationary floor and third-moment cap on all subsets of balls of radius L/96.
Fixed-amplitude, exactly matched radial counterexample in a regime where relative conductance discrepancy is uniformly exponentially small.
